previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of cholangiocarcinoma and recurrent biliary stent infections, was admitted with fever and chills concerning for cholangitis. He underwent an urgent ERCP, which was complicated by acute hemorrhage from a likely portobiliary fistula, resulting in a hemoglobin drop from 11.3 to 7.5 g/dL. He was stabilized with IV fluids and one unit of packed red blood cells, then transferred to the ICU. A portal vein stent was successfully placed to seal the fistula. Blood cultures grew ESBL-producing E. coli, sensitive to meropenem, and he was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to ertapenem. His infection resolved, and he was discharged home with plans to complete a 14-day antibiotic course and restart suppressive therapy with delafloxacin and fosfomycin. Follow-up was arranged with oncology and primary care.

anesthetic effect.  Under continuous ultrasound guidance and using a spacer on
the coaxial needle, an 18 gauge core biopsy device with a 22 mm throw was used
to obtain two core biopsy specimens, which were sent for pathology and
culture.  A minute amount of serosanguineous fluid was also aspirated from the
lesion and also sent for culture.

The procedure was tolerated well and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

SEDATION:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
1.5 mg Versed and 75 mcg fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of
35 minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.

An approximately 0.7 cm hypoechoic lesion with a punctate internal hyperechoic

to a questionable abscess seen on prior CT study from ___.  This
was targeted for biopsy and aspiration.

Successful core biopsy and aspiration of a 0.7 cm right hepatic lesion. 
Samples were sent for pathology and microbiology.
